questions.text: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: One newton is the force that gives a mass of one kilogram an acceleration of one metre per second squared.

questions.text: The SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature is the
questions.explanation: Kelvin is one of the seven SI base units; Celsius and Fahrenheit are derived or non-SI temperature scales.

questions.text: The SI unit of frequency is the
questions.explanation: One hertz corresponds to one complete cycle or vibration per second.

questions.text: Electrical resistance is measured in
questions.explanation: A conductor has a resistance of one ohm when a potential difference of one volt drives a current of one ampere through it.

questions.text: Which of the following is a base quantity in the SI system?
questions.explanation: Luminous intensity, measured in candela, is one of the seven SI base quantities; the others listed are derived quantities.

questions.text: A light year is a unit of
questions.explanation: A light year is the distance travelled by light in vacuum in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometres.

questions.text: One horsepower is approximately equal to
questions.explanation: The mechanical horsepower is defined as about 746 watts of power.

questions.text: The commercial unit of electrical energy used on domestic bills is the
questions.explanation: Electricity meters record energy in kilowatt-hours, where one kilowatt-hour equals 3.6 million joules.

questions.text: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement specifies both how far and in which direction, so it is a vector; the others have magnitude only.

questions.text: Atmospheric pressure is measured with a
questions.explanation: A barometer balances the weight of the atmosphere against a column of mercury or a sealed metal cell.

questions.text: The instrument used to measure the humidity of air is the
questions.explanation: A hygrometer indicates the amount of water vapour present in the air.

questions.text: Wind speed is measured by an
questions.explanation: An anemometer, usually a set of rotating cups, measures the speed of the wind.

questions.text: In a circuit, an ammeter is always connected
options: between the live and neutral wires
questions.explanation: An ammeter has very low resistance and must carry the whole current, so it is joined in series.

questions.text: A screw gauge is chiefly used to measure
options: the diameter of a thin wire
questions.explanation: A screw gauge, or micrometer, measures very small thicknesses and diameters to a fraction of a millimetre.

questions.text: The relative density of a liquid is measured with a
questions.explanation: A hydrometer floats at a depth that depends on the density of the liquid, and the scale reads relative density directly.

questions.text: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the law of
questions.explanation: The first law states that a body keeps its state of rest or uniform motion unless an external force acts, which is the property of inertia.

questions.text: The relation F = ma is a statement of Newton's
questions.explanation: The second law states that the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force, giving F = ma for constant mass.

questions.text: The backward recoil of a gun when it is fired is explained by the
questions.explanation: The total momentum before firing is zero, so the forward momentum of the bullet is balanced by an equal backward momentum of the gun.

questions.text: The momentum of a moving body is the product of its
questions.explanation: Linear momentum is defined as mass multiplied by velocity, and it is a vector quantity.

questions.text: The acceleration due to gravity near the surface of the Earth is about
questions.explanation: The standard value of g at the Earth's surface is 9.8 metres per second squared.

questions.text: The value of the acceleration due to gravity on Earth is greatest at
questions.explanation: The Earth is flattened at the poles, so the surface there is nearer the centre and g is largest.

questions.text: The weight of an object on the Moon is about
options: one-sixth of its weight on Earth
one-third of its weight on Earth
equal to its weight on Earth
six times its weight on Earth
questions.explanation: Gravity on the Moon is roughly one-sixth of that on Earth, so the same mass weighs about one-sixth as much.

questions.text: A body moving in a circle at constant speed has an acceleration directed
options: towards the centre of the circle
away from the centre of the circle
opposite to the direction of motion
questions.explanation: The velocity changes direction continuously, and the resulting centripetal acceleration always points towards the centre.

questions.text: The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is approximately
questions.explanation: A body must be projected at about 11.2 kilometres per second to escape the Earth's gravitational pull.

questions.text: The orbital period of a geostationary satellite is
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite completes one orbit in 24 hours so that it keeps pace with the Earth's rotation and appears fixed in the sky.

questions.text: According to Newton's law of gravitation, the force between two bodies is inversely proportional to
options: the square of the distance between them
the cube of the distance between them
questions.explanation: Gravitational attraction follows an inverse square law, falling to one quarter when the separation is doubled.

questions.text: The work done by a force is zero when the angle between the force and the displacement is
questions.explanation: Work equals force times displacement times the cosine of the angle, and cosine of 90 degrees is zero.

questions.text: One joule of work is done when a force of one newton moves a body through
questions.explanation: The joule is defined as one newton-metre, the work done by a force of one newton acting over a distance of one metre.

questions.text: The kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with speed v is given by
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy equals one half of the mass multiplied by the square of the speed.

questions.text: If the speed of a moving car is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is proportional to the square of the speed, so doubling the speed multiplies the energy by four.

questions.text: Water stored in a dam at a height possesses mainly
questions.explanation: Because of its raised position the water holds gravitational potential energy, which converts to kinetic energy as it falls.

questions.text: The law of conservation of energy states that energy
options: is always increasing in the universe
can be created but not destroyed
can neither be created nor destroyed but only changed in form
questions.explanation: Energy can only be transformed from one form to another; the total energy of an isolated system stays constant.

questions.text: An electric generator converts
questions.explanation: A generator rotates a coil in a magnetic field, so mechanical work is turned into electrical energy by induction.

questions.text: An electric motor converts electrical energy mainly into
questions.explanation: Current in a coil placed in a magnetic field experiences a turning force, producing mechanical rotation.

questions.text: The mechanical advantage of a machine is the ratio of
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage is the load overcome divided by the effort applied; the ratio of outputs to inputs of work is the efficiency.

questions.text: A wheelbarrow is an example of a lever of the
questions.explanation: In a wheelbarrow the load lies between the fulcrum at the wheel and the effort at the handles, which defines a second-class lever.

questions.text: The chief advantage of a single fixed pulley is that it
options: changes the direction of the effort
halves the load to be lifted
questions.explanation: A single fixed pulley has a mechanical advantage of one, so it only lets the effort be applied downward instead of upward.

questions.text: A screw may be regarded as a modified form of
questions.explanation: The thread of a screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder.

questions.text: The efficiency of an actual machine is always less than 100 per cent because
options: the load is always greater than the effort
some energy is wasted against friction
energy is destroyed inside the machine
the mechanical advantage is always less than one
questions.explanation: Part of the work input is converted into heat by friction, so the useful work output is smaller than the input.

questions.text: Absolute zero of temperature corresponds to
questions.explanation: Zero kelvin, the lowest possible temperature, is about -273 degrees Celsius.

questions.text: A temperature of 27 degrees Celsius is equal to
questions.explanation: Kelvin temperature is obtained by adding 273 to the Celsius reading, so 27 + 273 = 300 K.

questions.text: The Celsius and Fahrenheit scales show the same numerical reading at
questions.explanation: Solving C = (9C/5) + 32 gives C = -40, the single temperature at which both scales agree.

questions.text: Heat travels through a solid metal rod mainly by
questions.explanation: In solids energy passes from particle to particle without bulk movement of matter, which is conduction.

questions.text: Heat reaches the Earth from the Sun by the process of
questions.explanation: Radiation is the only mode of heat transfer that needs no material medium, so it can cross the vacuum of space.

questions.text: Which metal is the best conductor of heat?
questions.explanation: Silver has the highest thermal conductivity of all metals, slightly above copper.

questions.text: The specific heat capacity of water is about
questions.explanation: About 4200 joules are needed to raise the temperature of one kilogram of water by one kelvin, an unusually high value.

questions.text: Water has its maximum density at a temperature of
questions.explanation: Water contracts on cooling only down to 4 degrees Celsius and then expands, so it is densest at that temperature.

questions.text: Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because the increased pressure
options: lowers the boiling point of water
increases the specific heat of water
raises the boiling point of water
reduces the latent heat of steam
questions.explanation: Higher pressure inside the cooker allows water to boil above 100 degrees Celsius, so cooking proceeds at a higher temperature.

questions.text: Evaporation of a liquid always produces
options: a rise in temperature of the remaining liquid
an increase in the mass of the liquid
questions.explanation: The fastest molecules escape first and carry away energy, lowering the average energy and hence the temperature of what remains.

questions.text: A bimetallic strip bends on heating because the two metals
questions.explanation: The metal with the larger coefficient of linear expansion lengthens more, forcing the strip to curve.

questions.text: Sound waves travelling through air are
questions.explanation: Air particles vibrate back and forth along the direction of travel, producing compressions and rarefactions.

questions.text: Sound cannot travel through
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium, so it cannot pass through a vacuum.

questions.text: The speed of sound in air at 0 degrees Celsius is about
questions.explanation: Sound travels through air at roughly 332 metres per second at freezing point and slightly faster as the air warms.

questions.text: Sound travels fastest in
questions.explanation: Solids are the most elastic and closely packed media, so sound waves pass through them most rapidly.

questions.text: The normal range of audible frequencies for a healthy human ear is
questions.explanation: Frequencies below 20 hertz are infrasonic and those above 20,000 hertz are ultrasonic, both inaudible to humans.

questions.text: An echo is produced by the
questions.explanation: Sound bouncing back from a distant hard surface reaches the listener after a delay and is heard as a separate sound.

questions.text: The pitch of a musical note depends on its
questions.explanation: A higher frequency of vibration is perceived as a higher pitch.

questions.text: The intensity level of sound is commonly measured in
questions.explanation: The decibel is a logarithmic unit used to compare sound intensity levels.

questions.text: SONAR, used to find the depth of the sea, works by sending out
questions.explanation: SONAR emits ultrasonic pulses and times their echo from the sea bed to calculate depth.

questions.text: The apparent rise in the pitch of a train whistle as the train approaches a listener is called the
questions.explanation: Relative motion between source and observer changes the observed frequency, an effect named after Christian Doppler.

questions.text: The speed of light in vacuum is about
questions.explanation: Light travels at approximately 300,000 kilometres per second, that is 3 × 10^8 metres per second.

questions.text: Light from the Sun takes about how long to reach the Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is about 150 million kilometres away, so its light takes roughly eight minutes and twenty seconds to arrive.

questions.text: The image formed by a plane mirror is always
options: virtual and of the same size as the object
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms an upright virtual image as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, and of equal size.

questions.text: The rear-view mirror of a motor vehicle is
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always gives an erect diminished image and covers a wider field of view behind the vehicle.

questions.text: Refraction of light occurs because light
options: changes its speed in going from one medium to another
changes its colour in a new medium
is absorbed by the second medium
questions.explanation: A change of speed at the boundary makes the ray bend unless it strikes the surface normally.

questions.text: The refractive index of water is about
questions.explanation: Light travels about 1.33 times more slowly in water than in vacuum; 1.5 is typical of glass and 2.42 of diamond.

questions.text: Optical fibres transmit light signals over long distances by means of
questions.explanation: Light striking the core-cladding boundary beyond the critical angle is reflected entirely back into the core.

questions.text: The splitting of white light into its component colours by a glass prism is called
questions.explanation: Different colours have different refractive indices in glass, so they emerge at different angles as a spectrum.

questions.text: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Red light lies at the long wavelength end of the visible spectrum and violet at the short wavelength end.

questions.text: The blue colour of the clear daytime sky is caused by
options: absorption of red light by ozone
refraction of light in the atmosphere
scattering of sunlight by air molecules
questions.explanation: Short wavelengths are scattered far more strongly by tiny air molecules, so scattered blue light reaches the eye from all directions.

questions.text: The image formed on the retina of the human eye is
questions.explanation: The eye lens converges light to form a real inverted image on the retina, which the brain interprets as upright.

questions.text: Short-sightedness, or myopia, is corrected by using
questions.explanation: A diverging concave lens moves the image back onto the retina for a myopic eye that focuses light in front of it.

questions.text: The power of a lens is measured in
questions.explanation: Lens power is the reciprocal of the focal length in metres and its unit is the dioptre.

questions.text: The three primary colours of light are
questions.explanation: Red, green and blue light combine in different proportions to produce all other colours, including white.

questions.text: Which of the following electromagnetic radiations has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays lie at the extreme high-frequency end of the electromagnetic spectrum and so have the shortest wavelength.

questions.text: X-rays were discovered by
questions.explanation: Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and received the first Nobel Prize in Physics for the work.

questions.text: Ohm's law is expressed by the relation
questions.explanation: For a conductor at constant temperature the potential difference equals the current multiplied by the resistance.

questions.text: The resistance of a metallic wire of uniform material
options: depends only on the current through it
does not depend on its length
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area.

questions.text: Domestic electrical appliances are connected to the mains supply
questions.explanation: Parallel connection gives every appliance the same full voltage and lets each be switched on or off independently.

questions.text: The wire used in an electric fuse should have
options: a high melting point and low resistance
a low melting point and high resistance
a high melting point and high resistance
a low melting point and zero resistance
questions.explanation: A fuse wire must heat up quickly and melt before the excessive current can damage the circuit.

questions.text: Which element is widely used as a semiconductor in electronic devices?
questions.explanation: Silicon has a conductivity between that of conductors and insulators and forms the basis of diodes, transistors and chips.

questions.text: The magnitude of the charge on an electron is about
questions.explanation: The elementary charge is 1.6 × 10^-19 coulomb; 9.1 × 10^-31 kilogram is the electron's mass.

questions.text: The direction of conventional current in a circuit is
options: the same as the direction of electron flow
undefined in a direct current circuit
always from negative to positive outside the cell
opposite to the direction of electron flow
questions.explanation: Conventional current is taken to flow from the positive to the negative terminal, whereas electrons drift the other way.

questions.text: The filament of an ordinary electric bulb is made of
questions.explanation: Tungsten has a very high melting point and high resistivity, so it glows brightly without melting.

questions.text: A transformer can work only with
options: both direct and alternating current equally
questions.explanation: A transformer depends on a continuously changing magnetic flux, which only alternating current can provide.

questions.text: The working of an electric generator is based on the principle of
questions.explanation: Faraday showed that an electromotive force is induced whenever the magnetic flux linked with a coil changes.

questions.text: When two like poles of magnets are brought close together, they
questions.explanation: Like magnetic poles repel while unlike poles attract.

questions.text: A bar magnet suspended freely so that it can turn will finally come to rest pointing
questions.explanation: The Earth's magnetic field turns the magnet until its poles line up roughly along the north-south direction.

questions.text: The core of an electromagnet is usually made of soft iron because soft iron
options: loses its magnetism as soon as the current stops
questions.explanation: Soft iron is easily magnetised and demagnetised, which is exactly what a temporary electromagnet requires.

questions.text: The neutron was discovered by
questions.explanation: Chadwick identified the uncharged nuclear particle in 1932 and was awarded the Nobel Prize for it.

questions.text: The existence of the atomic nucleus was established by the alpha particle scattering experiment performed under
questions.explanation: Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed that the atom's positive charge and nearly all its mass are concentrated in a tiny nucleus.

questions.text: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of
questions.explanation: The atomic number is the count of protons, which fixes the identity of the element.

questions.text: The mass number of an atom is the total number of
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons are the nucleons, and together they account for almost the whole mass of the atom.

questions.text: Isotopes of the same element differ from one another in the number of
questions.explanation: Isotopes share the same atomic number but have different numbers of neutrons and hence different mass numbers.

questions.text: An alpha particle is identical with the nucleus of an atom of
questions.explanation: An alpha particle consists of two protons and two neutrons, which is a helium nucleus.

questions.text: Of the three main types of nuclear radiation, the most penetrating is
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are uncharged electromagnetic waves and need thick lead or concrete to be stopped, while alpha is stopped by paper.

questions.text: Radioactivity was first discovered by
questions.explanation: Becquerel found in 1896 that uranium salts emitted penetrating radiation without any external stimulus.

questions.text: The energy radiated by the Sun is produced by
questions.explanation: Hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium in the Sun's core, releasing enormous energy from the small loss of mass.

questions.text: The half-life of a radioactive element is the time in which
questions.explanation: Half-life is the time taken for half the radioactive nuclei present in a sample to disintegrate.

questions.text: Archimedes' principle states that a body immersed in a fluid experiences an upthrust equal to the
questions.explanation: The loss in apparent weight of the body equals the weight of the fluid it pushes aside.

questions.text: Hydraulic brakes in vehicles work on the principle stated by
questions.explanation: Pascal's law says pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions, so a small force at the pedal produces a large force at the wheels.

questions.text: The density of pure water is about
questions.explanation: One cubic metre of water has a mass of about 1000 kilograms, that is one gram per cubic centimetre.

questions.text: Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level supports a mercury column of
questions.explanation: Normal atmospheric pressure balances a column of mercury 760 millimetres, or 76 centimetres, high.

questions.text: The lift on the wing of an aeroplane in flight is explained by
questions.explanation: Air moves faster over the curved upper surface, lowering the pressure there, and the pressure difference produces upward lift.

questions.text: The mass of an electron is roughly what fraction of the mass of a proton?
questions.explanation: A proton is about 1836 times heavier than an electron.

questions.text: Friction between two sliding surfaces can be reduced by
options: increasing the load pressing them together
increasing the area of contact only
questions.explanation: A lubricant forms a thin layer that keeps the surfaces apart and lowers the force of sliding friction.

questions.text: The pressure exerted by a solid block on the ground can be reduced by
options: increasing the weight of the block
tilting the block on one edge
questions.explanation: Pressure is force divided by area, so spreading the same weight over a larger area lowers the pressure.

questions.text: According to Newton's third law of motion, action and reaction are equal and opposite but
options: cancel each other out on one body
act only when the bodies are in contact
questions.explanation: Because the two forces act on different bodies they never cancel, which is why motion can result.

questions.text: The force of gravity acting on a body is called its
questions.explanation: Weight is a force measured in newtons and equals mass multiplied by the acceleration due to gravity.

questions.text: A steel ship floats on water although steel is denser than water because
options: the ship is hollow and displaces a large weight of water
steel becomes lighter in sea water
sea water has a lower density than fresh water
the engines push the ship upward
questions.explanation: The hollow hull makes the average density of the ship less than that of water, so the upthrust can balance its weight.
